SRC-015:R001.text: Wave C/5 -- one shared audit enqueue producer API: monotonic allocator that never reuses deleted gaps, atomic temp-then-place write, idempotent retry on producer_operation_id, no arbitrary path and no overwrite of an existing layer

SRC-015:R002.text: Wave D/7 -- producer-neutral audit envelope: optional stable metadata header (audit_schema, producer, producer_version, producer_item_id, created_at, severity, confidence, observed_project, related/amends, maintainer_verdict) parsed without semantic interpretation of the body

SRC-015:R003.text: Wave E/7 -- maintainer disposition loop: producer identity survives intake, the audit->SRC->Work->disposition trace survives file deletion, and a compact read-only result projection is available to the producer

SRC-015:R004.text: Wave F -- multi-producer/concurrency hardening: narrow writer lock around allocation and final placement only, no partial final bytes visible to the consumer, and an idempotent crash matrix

SRC-015:R005.text: Wave G -- operator surface completion: `saipen status` carries a compact audit_inbox summary (pending, active layer, bound receipt, bound Work, closed-pending-delete, invalid, last allocated id) without dumping audit body text

SRC-015:R006.text: Wave H/7 -- SAIPAL bridge contract: SAIPAL receives only the constrained enqueue capability plus the read-only disposition lookup, with no Core/BOARD/STATE/LOG write and no producer-specific semantic branch in SAIPEN

SRC-015:R007.text: Wave 6 -- real HUSH runtime: `hush <task>` activates a task-local execution policy that suppresses discretionary narration only, leaves command meaning, phase lifecycle, tool effects and mandatory interaction unchanged, and does not leak into the next task

SRC-015:R008.text: Wave I -- dogfood and final hardening: manual, AUDAPACK-style and SAIPAL-like producers each drive the full discover->capture->normalize->Work->evidence->close->delete loop, including changed-generation, active-Work precedence, concurrent enqueue, rejection and crash recovery

SRC-015:R009.text: Wave 8 -- backlog re-entry: BOARD scrub of terminal historical detail, safe LOG seal at a checkpoint, disposition of stale producer packages through the existing collect/discard contracts, and automatic resumption of ordinary Pick Rule work once the inbox is empty
